eventMetadata.context_description: Manila’s late dry-season climatology and recent PAGASA observations favor a daily high near 33 °C on May 18, the market’s leading outcome at 37 % implied probability. Persistent high-pressure ridging over Luzon has sustained strong solar heating and urban heat-island amplification, yet increasing boundary-layer moisture is already producing scattered afternoon convection that caps peak temperatures. Ensemble guidance from global models shows only modest day-to-day variability, with most solutions clustering between 32–34 °C; a clear-sky breakout could push readings to 35 °C, while enhanced thunderstorm activity would likely hold the maximum at or below 33 °C. The next PAGASA bulletin and updated 48-hour model runs will provide the clearest signal before resolution.
